Third, regarding the causes for losing the vows, there is the general explanation and the analysis of whether or not the root downfalls are causes for losing the vows. 

Regarding the first: there is the way <term>Pratimoksha</term> is lost and, as a side discussion, the way the <term>Dhyana</term> and uncontaminated vows are lost. 

First, the <term>Pratimoksha</term> vow is lost by returning the trainings, because one has accepted the side that is incompatible with the vow. It is lost by dying, because the duration of the commitment has passed. It is lost by the simultaneous appearance of both genders or by the changing of gender three times, because the physical basis of the vow is impaired. It is lost by the severing of the roots of virtue, because the supporting basis for the vow no longer exists. The <term>Upavasa</term> <gloss>one-day</gloss> vow is lost once the final moment of the night has passed, because the duration of the commitment has expired. 

The <term>Sautrantika</term> <gloss>Sutra-Followers</gloss> school says that the vow is also lost by committing a root downfall with concealment, because the mental continuum is then dominated by a lack of shame and a lack of connection to the vow. The <term>Tamrashatiya</term> <gloss>those in red robes</gloss> school says it is lost when the scriptural Dharma disappears, because at that time the established boundaries of the training no longer exist.
